instructions: Put the 1 1/2 cups rice in a sieve and rinse it under cold water, swirling it with your hand, until the water runs almost clear. Leave it in the sieve to drain.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and slice the scallions, white and green parts. Finely chop the 3 garlic cloves. Chop the dill, leaving out the thick stalks. That should be about 1/2 cup.
Finely grate the zest of one lemon, then juice both lemons. That should be about 1/3 cup juice.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a wide, deep pan with a lid over medium heat. Add the onion, the scallions and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring now and then, until they're soft and see-through, about 5 minutes. Don't rush them.
Add the garlic, the lemon zest and the 1/2 tsp cumin. Stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the spinach a big handful at a time, stirring each one in until it collapses before you add the next. All of it takes about 4 minutes.
Stir in the drained rice, the 3 cups broth, half the dill, 3/4 tsp salt and a few grinds of pepper. Turn the heat up to high and bring it to a boil.

Turn the heat down to low, cover, and simmer for about 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and has taken up nearly all the broth. Stir it once halfway so the bottom doesn't catch. If it looks dry before the rice is done, add a splash of hot water.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the lemon juice, the rest of the dill and the last 1 tbsp olive oil. It should be soft and a little loose.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt and another grind of pepper.
Serve with the 4 oz feta crumbled over the top.
method_notes: All the versions soften onion (and scallion or leek) in olive oil, wilt a lot of spinach, simmer rice in about two cups of liquid per cup of rice, and finish with dill and lemon, with feta on top for most. A Family Feast (the lead) is the lemon version: lemon zest and cumin go in with the spinach, the rice simmers in broth with half the dill, and the juice and remaining dill go in at the end. My Greek Dish adds tomato and tomato paste and Diane Kochilas adds fennel and a long 45 minute simmer; this follows the lead, scaled up by half to make a dinner for four, with the scallions both other versions use, a spoon of olive oil to finish as Kochilas does, and the feta the other two serve it with.
